newsitem.title: UK: United Utilities warns of windfall tax review.
newsitem.headline: United Utilities warns of windfall tax review.

text.p: UK multi-utility United Utilities Plc said on Friday the imposition of a one-off tax on excess profits would trigger a "comprehensive review" of discretionary revenue and capital expenditure, customer rebates and voluntary compensation schemes.
"This comprehensive review will be from top down, what the customer values most, and bottom up, as to what the company can afford," chairman Sir Desmond Pitcher told the annual meeting.
He added that savings in the group's utility division were "a little ahead of budget," while in the international division, earnings "have been slower to come through than originally anticipated."
The one-off tax on the excess profits of privatised utilities, known as the windfall tax, was introduced by the new Labour government in its first budget on July 2.
United Utilities has given no official figures for its share of the tax, aimed at raising a total 5.2 billion stg.
Pitcher added that although international earnings were slower, projected earnings are "of a higher quality and absorb less capital."

On Monday, the company courted controversy when it unexpectedly sacked its chief executive, Brian Staples, and warned that current trade was slightly below expectations, prompting some analysts to suggest overseas operations could have more lacklustre results.
Derek Green was appointed as the new chief executive from his post as managing director of the group's utility division.
The company's shares slumped on Monday when Staples was fired, to close at 702 pence, but have recovered during the week to stand at 731.5 pence by 1020 GMT on Friday, up half a penny.
